candidate.educational_objective: Prevent peristomal irritant injury by ensuring a close-fitting barrier opening and promptly changing a leaking pouching system.

options.A: Apply an oily moisturizing cream under the skin barrier at each change because a lubricated surface improves pouch adhesion.
options.B: Re-measure the stoma and fit the barrier opening closely around its base, changing the system promptly when leakage or burning occurs rather than reinforcing a leak.
options.C: Cut the barrier opening noticeably larger than the stoma so a rim of peristomal skin remains exposed to stool beneath the pouch.
options.D: Keep a leaking pouch in place until the routine change day because continued stool exposure is less damaging than an unscheduled system change.

candidate.rationale: WOCN’s Peristomal Skin Assessment Guide advises that the skin barrier opening should fit closely around the stoma and that a pouching system should be changed when leakage, burning, or itching occurs rather than reinforced over a leak. These steps reduce effluent contact with peristomal skin and directly address the client’s symptoms.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A close-fitting skin barrier and prompt system change for leakage/burning help prevent stool/effluent contact with peristomal skin.
